docs.title: Welcome to SENTINEL
docs.text: SENTINEL is an Autonomous Multi-Agent Digital Forensics and Incident Response (DFIR) Platform designed to automate security incident triage, multi-domain evidence correlation, and threat containment without exposing sensitive enterprise telemetry to public cloud AI APIs.

docs.title: 🎯 The Core Problem
docs.text:
Modern Security Operations Centers (SOCs) are overwhelmed by two systemic challenges:

  1. Alert Fatigue & Cognitive Overload: Tier-1 and Tier-2 security analysts triage between 500 and 1,000 alerts daily. Over 80% are false positives or disconnected point-in-time alerts (e.g., an alert from the firewall, an alert from the endpoint, and an alert from the email gateway). Analysts must spend 30 to 60 minutes manually stitching disparate logs together to understand the root cause of an intrusion.
  2. Data Privacy & Legal Privilege Breaches: Forensic telemetry (memory images, PCAP network captures, Windows event logs, and email bodies) frequently contains unhashed passwords, customer PII, cryptographic keys, and proprietary corporate secrets. Routing this data to commercial cloud AI models (such as OpenAI GPT-4, Google Gemini, or Microsoft Copilot) violates strict data privacy standards (GDPR, HIPAA, SOC 2) and compromises legal attorney-client privilege during corporate breach litigation.

docs.title: 💡 The SENTINEL Solution
docs.text:
SENTINEL eliminates this trade-off by deploying an entirely local, air-gapped multi-agent investigation system:

  • Zero Data Egress: All models run locally via Ollama (llama3.1), vector embeddings run on-premise with ChromaDB, and cases are tracked in an embedded SQLite database.
  • Deterministic + Probabilistic Guardrails: Before any LLM reasoning takes place, raw evidence is evaluated against hardened Sigma YAML rules and compiled YARA signatures to eliminate false-negative dropouts for known threats.
  • Specialized Multi-Agent Collaboration: Implemented as a LangGraph Directed Acyclic Graph (DAG), specialized sub-agents independently evaluate their domain (Endpoint, Network, Memory, Phishing) before feeding into a Lead SOC Correlation Analyst that deduces attack causality.
  • Actionable Closed-Loop Response: Automatically synthesizes custom SOAR containment playbooks (netsh, iptables, EDR API calls), multi-dialect SIEM threat hunting queries (Splunk SPL, Sentinel KQL, Elastic EQL), and structured Jira / ServiceNow incident tickets.

docs.title: 1. Multi-Source Forensic Ingestion
docs.text:
SENTINEL natively extracts, normalizes, and correlates evidence across all primary forensic domains:

Artifact Type File Formats Forensic Extractions Endpoint Logs .evtx Process execution (4688), User logon sessions (4624/4625), Service installations (7045), PowerShell ScriptBlock execution (4104) Network Streams .pcap, .cap HTTP request/response payloads, Shannon entropy DNS tunneling detection, statistical C2 beacon volume clustering Memory Images .mem, .raw, .vmem Volatility 3 integration for active processes (pslist), socket connections (netscan), and in-RAM code injections (malfind) Email Forensics .eml SPF/DKIM header authentication auditing, sender spoofing detection, malicious URL extraction, attachment MD5 hashing

docs.title: 2. Multi-Agent LangGraph Pipeline
docs.text: A coordinated team of autonomous agents operating under a strictly validated schema: - 💻 Endpoint Analyst Agent: Evaluates EVTX logs, Sigma detections, and process trees. - 🌐 Network Analyst Agent: Inspects DNS tunneling anomalies, HTTP requests, and C2 beacons. - 🧠 Memory Analyst Agent: Analyzes process hollowing and RAM injections. - 📧 Email / Phishing Analyst Agent: Analyzes social engineering tactics and credential harvesting lures. - ⚡ Lead SOC Correlation Agent: Synthesizes domain findings into a unified, chronological attack narrative. - 🛡️ SOAR Remediation Agent: Generates immediate firewall blocking rules and EDR isolation commands. - 🔍 SIEM Threat Hunter: Auto-authors ready-to-deploy Splunk SPL, Azure KQL, and Elastic EQL hunting queries. - 🎫 Automated Ticketing Engine: Generates structured Jira and ServiceNow incident payloads.

docs.title: 3. Interactive SOC Dashboard
docs.text: A 9-tab interactive command center powered by Streamlit: - 📊 Interactive Timeline: Plotly Gantt scatter chart displaying chronologically sequenced forensic events. - 🔗 Attack Relationship Graph: Force-directed Vis.js network graph connecting hosts, user accounts, and IOCs. - 🎯 IOCs & MITRE TTPs: Extracted indicators and dynamic ATT&CK technique badges. - 🌍 Threat Intel Integration: On-demand reputation lookups with VirusTotal and AbuseIPDB. - 🔐 STIX 2.1 Export: Downloadable OASIS CTI bundles for automated threat sharing.

docs.title: SENTINEL Architecture & Multi-Agent Flow
docs.text: SENTINEL utilizes a modular, multi-agent AI architecture built on LangGraph. By decomposing complex forensic investigations into specialized sub-agents with strict deterministic guardrails, SENTINEL avoids prompt context exhaustion, minimizes hallucinations, and maintains auditable causality chains across multiple forensic domains.

docs.title: 🏗️ High-Level State Machine (LangGraph DAG)
docs.text:
The core orchestration engine operates as a Directed Acyclic Graph (DAG) using a shared, strictly typed AgentState:

flowchart TD
    subgraph INGESTION["1. Heterogeneous Ingestion & Deterministic Layer"]
        RAW["Uploaded Telemetry (.evtx, .pcap, .mem, .eml)"] --> PARSER["Parser Node"]
        PARSER --> SIGMA["Sigma Rule Engine (YAML)"]
        PARSER --> YARA["YARA Scanner (.yar)"]
        PARSER --> NORM["ForensicArtifact Normalization (Pydantic)"]
    end

    subgraph RAG_KB["Local Knowledge Retrieval Layer"]
        CHROMA[("ChromaDB Vector Store\n(MITRE ATT&CK STIX 2.1)")]
        NORM -.-> |Semantic Similarity| CHROMA
    end

    subgraph DOMAIN_AGENTS["2. Domain-Specific Forensic Agents (Fan-Out)"]
        NORM --> EP["Endpoint Analyst Agent\n(EVTX & Sigma Matches)"]
        NORM --> NET["Network Analyst Agent\n(PCAP, DNS Entropy, C2 Beacons)"]
        NORM --> MEM["Memory Analyst Agent\n(Volatility 3 & Injections)"]
        NORM --> EML["Email Analyst Agent\n(SPF/DKIM & Phishing Lures)"]
    end

    subgraph CORRELATION["3. Cognitive Synthesis & Correlation (Fan-In)"]
        EP --> LEAD["Lead SOC Correlation Agent\n(Multi-Domain Timeline Fusion)"]
        NET --> LEAD
        MEM --> LEAD
        EML --> LEAD
    end

    subgraph CLOSED_LOOP["4. Actionable Response Pipeline"]
        LEAD --> REP["Reporter Node\n(Markdown & STIX 2.1)"]
        REP --> SOAR["SOAR Remediation Agent\n(Netsh, Iptables, EDR API)"]
        SOAR --> HUNT["SIEM Threat Hunter\n(Splunk SPL, KQL, EQL)"]
        HUNT --> TICKET["Automated Ticketing Engine\n(Jira REST API JSON)"]
    end

    subgraph PRESENTATION["5. Presentation & SOC Dashboard"]
        TICKET --> UI["Streamlit SOC Dashboard"]
        UI --> GANTT["Plotly Chronological Timeline"]
        UI --> GRAPH["Vis.js Force-Directed Attack Graph"]
        UI --> SQLITE[("Persistent SQLite Archive\n(sentinel.db)")]
    end

docs.title: 1. Ingestion & Normalization (src/schema.py)
docs.text:
Incoming telemetry files are parsed and normalized into standard ForensicArtifact Pydantic models:

class ForensicArtifact(BaseModel):
    timestamp: str          # ISO 8601 normalized event timestamp
    source_type: str        # e.g., EVTX_4688, PCAP_DNS_TUNNEL, EML_URL
    host: Optional[str]     # Hostname or IP address
    user: Optional[str]     # Username or account identifier
    details: str            # Raw command line, DNS query, or header summary
    ioc_detected: Optional[str] # Extracted IP, domain, hash, or suspicious URL

docs.title: 2. Deterministic Guardrails (Sigma & YARA)
docs.text: To ensure reliable, auditable detection of known malicious indicators: * Sigma Engine (src/parsers/sigma_scanner.py): Ingests community YAML Sigma rules from rules/sigma/. Checks normalized EVTX event details for known adversarial techniques (e.g., encoded PowerShell execution, remote WMI process creation, volume shadow copy deletion). * YARA Engine (src/parsers/yara_scanner.py): Automatically compiles .yar signatures from rules/yara/ to scan memory dumps and file binaries for PsExec artifacts, lateral movement tools, and ransomware headers.

docs.title: 3. Local RAG & MITRE ATT&CK Mapping (src/kb/)
docs.text:
• Embedding Model: all-MiniLM-L6-v2 dense sentence representations running locally via sentence-transformers.
  • Vector Store: ChromaDB indexed against enterprise MITRE ATT&CK STIX 2.1 objects.
  • Operation: When suspicious activities are identified, SENTINEL performs semantic vector similarity queries to retrieve exact MITRE Technique IDs (e.g., T1059.001 - PowerShell, T1071.004 - DNS Tunneling, T1566.002 - Spearphishing Link).

docs.title: A. Domain Specialist Agents (Fan-Out)
docs.text:
Rather than overloading a single model with thousands of disparate logs, four dedicated sub-agents evaluate their specific forensic domains independently:

  1. 💻 Endpoint Analyst Agent:
  2. Examines Windows Security logs (Event IDs 4624, 4625, 4688, 4104, 7045).
  3. Evaluates parent-child process hierarchies and Sigma rule detections.

  4. Identifies privilege escalation, execution, and persistence techniques.

  5. 🌐 Network Analyst Agent:

  6. Computes Shannon Entropy over DNS query subdomains to flag high-entropy DNS tunneling tools (e.g., Iodine, DNSCat2).
  7. Parses HTTP streams to identify unencrypted credential transmissions and exfiltration payloads.

  8. Computes temporal connection counts to flag periodic Command and Control (C2) beacons.

  9. 🧠 Memory Analyst Agent:

  10. Evaluates Volatility 3 outputs (windows.pslist, windows.netscan, windows.malfind).

  11. Detects reflective DLL injection, process hollowing, and in-RAM YARA signature hits.

  12. 📧 Email / Phishing Analyst Agent:

  13. Audits RFC 5322 email headers for SPF (Received-SPF) and DKIM authentication failures.
  14. Extracts embedded hyperlink targets to uncover credential harvesting lures.
  15. Flags high-urgency social engineering patterns and suspicious file attachments.

docs.title: B. Lead SOC Correlation Agent (Fan-In)
docs.text:
The Lead SOC Analyst acts as the synthesis hub. It takes the summarized intelligence outputs from all four domain specialists and fuses them into a single, chronological attack story.

By reasoning over multi-source evidence, it establishes causality: $$\text{Phishing Lure} \xrightarrow{\text{Delivery}} \text{DNS Beacon} \xrightarrow{\text{C2 Established}} \text{Process Execution} \xrightarrow{\text{Privilege Escalation}} \text{Data Exfiltration}$$

docs.title: C. Closed-Loop Action Pipeline
docs.text:
Following correlation, SENTINEL automatically triggers proactive defensive actions:

  1. 🛡️ SOAR Remediation Agent:
  2. Synthesizes host firewall commands (netsh advfirewall for Windows, iptables for Linux).
  3. Formats REST API payloads for active EDR isolation (CrowdStrike Falcon, Microsoft Defender API).

  4. Generates custom Sigma and YARA rules to detect future occurrences of the observed threat.

  5. 🔍 SIEM Threat Hunter:

  6. Authors target hunting queries in Splunk SPL across index telemetry.
  7. Authors Microsoft Sentinel / Azure KQL queries targeting DeviceProcessEvents and DeviceNetworkEvents.

  8. Authors Elastic EQL queries to trace parent-child process chains and network connections.

  9. 🎫 Automated Ticketing Engine:

  10. Transforms incident findings, timelines, and remediation recommendations into a structured, validated Jira / ServiceNow REST API JSON payload.

docs.title: 💾 Forensic Data Lifecycle & SQLite Persistence
docs.text:
SENTINEL uses a persistent SQLite database (data/sentinel.db) with a data reduction architecture:

[ Raw Artifacts (temp_uploads/) ]  <-- Multi-gigabyte PCAP, EVTX, RAM dumps
               │
               ▼ (Extracted & Normalized)
[ Normalized ForensicArtifacts ]   <-- Structured Pydantic objects (KB size)
               │
               ▼ (Investigated & Correlated)
[ SQLite Database (data/sentinel.db) ] <-- Permanent Case Archive
               │
               ▼ (Instant Retrieval)
[ Dashboard "Case History" Replay ] <-- Instant reconstruction of charts and reports

docs.title: Storage Efficiency & Instant Replay
docs.text:
• 99.9% Data Reduction: Storing raw memory dumps or packet captures for every investigation is unsustainable. SENTINEL extracts high-value security evidence into serialized JSON strings in SQLite.
  • Zero Re-computation: When an archived case is opened in the dashboard, the pre-computed timelines, agent summaries, attack relationships, and reports are deserialized in milliseconds without re-invoking the LLM.

docs.title: 🛡️ Adding Custom YARA & Sigma Rules
docs.text: SENTINEL's parser node automatically discovers and compiles rules located in the rules/ directory.

docs.title: 1. Adding a YARA Rule
docs.text:
Drop any .yar or .yara file into rules/yara/. The engine compiles all files in the directory on startup.

Example: rules/yara/suspicious_dropper.yar 

rule Suspicious_Powershell_Dropper {
    meta:
        description = "Detects hidden download cradles in script files or memory"
        author = "SENTINEL SOC"
        mitre = "T1059.001"
    strings:
        $cradle1 = "Net.WebClient" ascii nocase
        $cradle2 = "DownloadString" ascii nocase
        $cradle3 = "IEX" ascii nocase
    condition:
        all of them
}

docs.title: 2. Adding a Sigma Rule
docs.text:
Drop any .yml or .yaml file into rules/sigma/.

Example: rules/sigma/process_injection.yml 

title: Potential Process Injection via CreateRemoteThread
id: e4b23c91-4d1a-4f9e-a89e-b9b9c9d9e9e9
description: Detects process injection attempts using suspicious utility binaries.
status: experimental
author: SENTINEL Threat Intel
tags:
    - attack.t1055
    - attack.privilege_escalation
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection:
        EventID: 4688
        CommandLine|contains: 'inject.exe'
    condition: selection
level: critical

docs.title: 🔌 Writing a New Forensic Parser
docs.text: To add support for a new evidence format (e.g., Linux Auditd, Zeek logs, or AWS CloudTrail):

docs.title: Step 1: Create the Parser in src/parsers/
docs.text:
Implement a function that accepts the evidence file path and returns a list of normalized ForensicArtifact objects:

# src/parsers/auditd_parser.py
import re
from datetime import datetime, timezone
from typing import List
from src.schema import ForensicArtifact

def parse_auditd(file_path: str) -> List[ForensicArtifact]:
    artifacts = []
    with open(file_path, "r", encoding="utf-8", errors="ignore") as f:
        for line in f:
            if "type=EXECVE" in line:
                # Extract command and timestamp
                artifacts.append(
                    ForensicArtifact(
                        timestamp=datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat(),
                        source_type="LINUX_AUDITD",
                        host="linux-server",
                        user="root",
                        details=f"Execve event: {line.strip()}",
                        ioc_detected=None
                    )
                )
    return artifacts

docs.title: Step 2: Register in src/agent/nodes.py
docs.text:
In parser_node(), wire the file extension to your new parser: 

elif fp.endswith(".audit") or fp.endswith(".log"):
    artifacts.extend(parse_auditd(fp))

docs.title: 🤖 Adding or Modifying LangGraph Agents
docs.text:
The multi-agent state is defined in src/agent/state.py using AgentState(TypedDict):

class AgentState(TypedDict):
    file_paths: List[str]
    llm_model: str
    artifacts: List[ForensicArtifact]
    endpoint_summary: str
    network_summary: str
    memory_summary: str
    email_summary: str
    timeline: str
    report: str
    remediation_plan: str
    threat_hunt_queries: str
    jira_ticket: str
    messages: Annotated[Sequence[BaseMessage], operator.add]

docs.title: Creating a New Agent Node
docs.text:
1. Define the node function in src/agent/nodes.py: 

    def cloud_analyst_node(state: AgentState):
    """Analyzes AWS CloudTrail or Azure Activity Logs."""
    chat = get_llm(state)
    sys_msg = SystemMessage(content="You are an expert Cloud Security Analyst...")
    user_msg = HumanMessage(content=f"Analyze these cloud artifacts: {state['artifacts']}")
    response = chat.invoke([sys_msg, user_msg])
    return {"cloud_summary": response.content}

  2. Register the node in src/agent/graph.py: 

    workflow.add_node("cloud_agent", cloud_analyst_node)
workflow.add_edge("parser", "cloud_agent")
workflow.add_edge("cloud_agent", "correlation")

docs.title: 🧪 Testing Guidelines
docs.text: SENTINEL enforces unit testing for all parsers and rule evaluations.

docs.title: Running Tests
docs.text: pytest -v

docs.title: Adding a Unit Test
docs.text:
Create tests in tests/test_<component>.py: 

def test_parse_custom_log(tmp_path):
    log_file = tmp_path / "test.log"
    log_file.write_text("type=EXECVE a0=sudo a1=bash\n")
    artifacts = parse_auditd(str(log_file))
    assert len(artifacts) == 1
    assert artifacts[0].source_type == "LINUX_AUDITD"

All contributions must pass pytest with zero warnings before merging.

docs.title: Competitive Differentiation & Endterm Roadmap
docs.text: This document outlines SENTINEL's unique scientific and engineering advantages over pre-existing cybersecurity platforms, followed by the week-by-week development roadmap leading to the final Endterm capstone defense.

docs.title: 🥊 How SENTINEL Differs from Pre-Existing Solutions
docs.text:
To understand SENTINEL's novelty, we benchmark it against the four prevailing paradigms in enterprise cybersecurity:

┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                               CYBERSECURITY ARCHITECTURES                              │
├────────────────────────┬────────────────────────┬──────────────────────────────────────┤
│ 1. Legacy SIEM / SOAR  │ 2. Cloud AI Copilots   │ 3. Raw DFIR Tools    │ 4. SENTINEL   │
│ (Splunk, Microsoft     │ (Microsoft Security    │ (Autopsy, FTK,       │ (Autonomous,  │
│ Sentinel, Cortex SOAR) │ Copilot, Charlotte AI) │ Volatility CLI)      │ Local Multi-  │
│                        │                        │                      │ Agent DFIR)   │
└────────────────────────┴────────────────────────┴──────────────────────┴───────────────┘

docs.title: 1. vs. Traditional SIEM & SOAR (Splunk, Microsoft Sentinel, Cortex XSOAR)
docs.text:
• The Problem: Traditional SIEMs are passive, rule-based log aggregation databases. During a multi-stage attack, they generate dozens of disconnected alerts (e.g., an alert from the firewall, an alert from Windows event logs, an alert from the email gateway). Human Tier-1/Tier-2 analysts must spend 45+ minutes manually stitching logs together into an incident story. SOAR playbooks are rigid Python scripts that break as soon as an attacker modifies minor command-line parameters.
  • The SENTINEL Advantage: SENTINEL is autonomous and generative. Instead of creating 10 disconnected alerts, it synthesizes the entire intrusion into a single, chronological causality narrative (e.g., "Attacker lured user via phishing email → established C2 beacon → executed PowerShell → exfiltrated credentials"), and dynamically authors custom containment rules (firewall, EDR API, Sigma).

docs.title: 2. vs. Cloud-Based AI Tools (Microsoft Security Copilot, CrowdStrike Charlotte AI)
docs.text:
• The Problem: Cloud Copilots send confidential enterprise telemetry over the WAN to commercial cloud LLMs. Incident response artifacts contain proprietary secrets, unhashed passwords, user PII, and sensitive network architecture. Sending this data to external APIs violates GDPR, HIPAA, SOC 2, and destroys legal attorney-client privilege during corporate breach litigation. Furthermore, they lock customers into proprietary ecosystems (Defender/Falcon).
  • The SENTINEL Advantage: 100% Privacy-Preserving and Air-Gapped. Zero bytes leave the machine. It runs entirely on local quantized open-weights models (Llama 3.1 via Ollama) and local vector embeddings (ChromaDB). It is vendor-agnostic and ingests raw open forensic standards (.evtx, .pcap, .mem, .eml).

docs.title: 3. vs. Forensic Suites (Autopsy, FTK Imager, Volatility)
docs.text:
• The Problem: These tools are extractors, not analyzers. They dump massive tables of raw data (e.g., 500 processes from pslist, thousands of raw packets in Wireshark) but cannot deduce intent, correlate across domains, or recommend defensive actions.
  • The SENTINEL Advantage: SENTINEL acts as a virtual Tier-2/Tier-3 forensic analyst team. It reasons over raw evidence, calculates entropy to identify DNS tunnels, extracts IOCs, matches MITRE ATT&CK techniques, and auto-generates SIEM queries and Jira tickets.

docs.title: 4. vs. Generic LLM Chatbots (ChatGPT / Prompt Wrappers)
docs.text:
• The Problem: Dumping raw logs into ChatGPT causes massive token exhaustion and dangerous hallucinations (inventing fake IP addresses or hallucinating attack stages).
  • The SENTINEL Advantage: Hybrid Deterministic-to-Probabilistic Guardrails. High-severity artifacts are first grounded against hardened Sigma and YARA rules before reaching the LLMs. The multi-agent fan-out ensures domain models stay focused on their specific telemetry.

docs.title: 📅 Sprint 1 (Weeks 1–2): Research Benchmarking & Quantitative Evaluation
docs.text:
• Objective: Transition from qualitative demonstrations to measurable, peer-reviewed evaluation metrics.
  • Key Tasks:
  • Benchmark Against Cyber Ranges: Curate automated evaluation pipelines against Splunk BOTS (Boss of the SOC) v1–v3, DARPA Transparent Computing (TC), and EVTX-ATTACK-SAMPLES.
  • Quantitative Performance Metrics:
    • TTP Classification Precision & Recall: Accuracy of mapped MITRE ATT&CK techniques against ground truth.
    • IOC Extraction Accuracy: Precision and Recall across IPs, domains, hashes, and URLs.
    • Mean Time to Correlate (MTTC): Compare SENTINEL's ~40-second analysis time against the human Tier-1/Tier-2 analyst baseline (~45 minutes).

docs.title: 📅 Sprint 2 (Weeks 3–4): Autonomous Agent Tool-Use & MCP Protocol
docs.text:
• Objective: Upgrade sub-agents from zero-shot prompting to active, interactive function-calling agents.
  • Key Tasks:
  • Interactive LangChain Tool Binding:
    • cyberchef_decode_base64(): Recursively deobfuscates nested PowerShell, XOR, or compressed payloads.
    • entropy_calculator(): Computes sliding-window Shannon entropy across packet streams.
    • whois_dns_lookup(): Local WHOIS/ASN resolution.
  • Model Context Protocol (MCP) Server Support: Expose SENTINEL's forensic parsers and graph intelligence as an MCP server, enabling external agentic workflows to query SENTINEL directly.

docs.title: 📅 Sprint 3 (Weeks 5–6): Big-Data Ingestion & Linux / Cloud Telemetry
docs.text:
• Objective: Expand ingestion capabilities to enterprise Linux and multi-cloud environments.
  • Key Tasks:
  • Streaming Packet Engine: Replace in-memory Scapy rdpcap with a streaming generator (pyshark / tshark chunking) to ingest multi-gigabyte PCAPs without memory spikes.
  • Linux Auditd & Syslog Parsers: Ingest /var/log/audit/audit.log and auth.log to detect sudo abuse, privilege escalation, and SSH brute-forcing.
  • AWS CloudTrail & Azure Activity Log Parsers: Ingest JSON audit logs to detect cloud IAM credential compromise and S3 bucket exfiltration.

docs.title: 📅 Sprint 4 (Weeks 7–8): Closed-Loop Adversary Emulation (Validation Harness)
docs.text:
• Objective: Empirically prove that SENTINEL's generated defenses block real-world attacks.
  • Key Tasks:
  • Atomic Red Team Integration:
    • Automated harness triggers an Atomic Red Team technique (e.g., T1047 WMI execution).
    • Telemetry is ingested by SENTINEL.
    • SENTINEL generates firewall blocking rules and Sigma detection signatures.
    • Test harness applies the generated rule and re-runs the attack to verify automated containment.

docs.title: 📅 Sprint 5 (Weeks 9–10): Production Packaging, Paper Writing & Final Defense
docs.text:
• Objective: Finalize production distribution and academic capstone thesis.
  • Key Tasks:
  • Single-Command Containerization: Re-introduce docker-compose up packaging orchestrating Streamlit, Ollama, ChromaDB, and SQLite.
  • Academic Paper / Thesis Draft: Complete formal IEEE/ACM conference-formatted capstone thesis: Abstract, Related Work, System Architecture, Benchmark Evaluation, and Case Studies.

docs.title: SENTINEL User Guide & Walkthrough
docs.text: This guide provides end-to-end instructions for deploying SENTINEL locally, conducting an autonomous multi-source forensic investigation, navigating the 9-tab dashboard, running automated CLI evaluations, and integrating with the REST API.

docs.title: 💻 Prerequisites & Local Setup
docs.text: SENTINEL is built for completely local, air-gapped execution. An Apple Silicon Mac (M1/M2/M3) or a machine with a dedicated GPU and 16GB+ RAM is recommended for optimal inference speed.

docs.title: Step 1: Clone the Repository
docs.text:
git clone https://github.com/udaygr0ver/SENTINEL.git
cd SENTINEL

docs.title: Step 2: Configure Python Virtual Environment
docs.text:
python3 -m venv venv
source venv/bin/activate  # On Windows: venv\Scripts\activate
pip install -r requirements.txt

docs.title: Step 3: Start Ollama & Pull Llama 3.1
docs.text:
Install Ollama if not already installed, ensure the Ollama daemon is running, and pull the default Llama 3.1 model: 

ollama pull llama3.1
(You can also pull mistral or llama3.1:70b if your hardware permits).

docs.title: 🚀 Running the Interactive SOC Dashboard
docs.text:
Launch the Streamlit web dashboard: 

streamlit run src/app.py
Open your browser and navigate to http://localhost:8501.

docs.title: 1. Upload Forensic Evidence
docs.text:
In the 🆕 New Investigation view, drag and drop one or more forensic evidence files into the upload zone: * .evtx (Windows Event Logs) * .pcap or .cap (Network Packet Captures) * .mem, .raw, or .vmem (Memory Dumps) * .eml (Phishing Email Files)

💡 Try the Pre-Packaged Demo Data: The repository includes verified attack fixtures in the demo_data/ folder: * demo_data/phishing_attack.eml: Spoofed Office 365 credential harvesting email with failed SPF/DKIM records. * demo_data/lateral_movement.pcap: Scapy capture containing high-entropy DNS tunneling and HTTP C2 beaconing. * demo_data/security_log.evtx: Real Windows Event Log containing suspicious process creations and logon sessions.

docs.title: 2. Configure Investigation Settings (Sidebar)
docs.text:
• LLM Model: Select llama3.1 (default), mistral, or larger parameter variants.
  • RAG Top-K Results: Adjust the number of MITRE ATT&CK techniques retrieved per suspicious event (default: 3).
  • Threat Intel APIs (Optional): Enter your VirusTotal and AbuseIPDB API keys to enable real-time reputation queries for extracted IOCs.

docs.title: 3. Execute Analysis
docs.text: Click 🚀 Run Analysis. The real-time progress bar will track the 7-agent pipeline: $$\text{Parser} \rightarrow \text{Domain Specialists} \rightarrow \text{Lead SOC Correlation} \rightarrow \text{SOAR} \rightarrow \text{Threat Hunter} \rightarrow \text{Ticketing}$$

docs.title: Tab 1: 📊 Timeline
docs.text:
• Plotly Interactive Gantt Chart: Displays timestamped forensic events across all source domains. Hover over data points to inspect raw command lines, URLs, and process names.
  • AI-Generated Narrative: The Lead SOC Analyst's correlated, chronological intrusion story detailing the initial access vector through to exfiltration.

docs.title: Tab 2: 🔗 Attack Graph
docs.text:
• Force-Directed Network Visualization: Built with streamlit-agraph / Vis.js.
  • Nodes:
  • 🔵 Hexagons (Hosts): Compromised workstations or servers.
  • 💎 Diamonds (Users): User accounts identified in logon or process events.
  • ⭐ Stars (IOCs): Malicious IPs, domains, hashes, and URLs.
  • 🟡 Circles (Global): Global scan or signature detections.
  • Physics Engine: Tuned repulsive physics allow dragging nodes and inspecting relationship edges without text overlap.

docs.title: Tab 3: 🤖 Agent Summaries
docs.text: A 2-column comparative layout displaying the individual intelligence summaries from each specialized agent: * 💻 Endpoint Analyst: Process anomalies, Sigma rule hits, privilege escalation attempts. * 🌐 Network Analyst: DNS tunneling anomalies, C2 beacon intervals, exfiltration targets. * 🧠 Memory Analyst: Volatility RAM analysis and injected code detection. * 📧 Email Analyst: Spoofed sender headers, failed SPF/DKIM records, and phishing lure tactics.

docs.title: Tab 4: 🎯 IOCs & Evidence
docs.text:
• IOC Badges: Extracted indicators of compromise ready for copying into firewall or proxy blocklists.
  • MITRE ATT&CK TTP Badges: Visual tags (e.g., ⚔️ T1059.001, ⚔️ T1071.004) dynamically extracted from Sigma and YARA findings.
  • Full Evidence Log: Chronological table of all parsed ForensicArtifact objects with source type, user, host, and details.

docs.title: Tab 5: 🌍 Threat Intel
docs.text:
• Real-time reputation lookups for extracted IOCs against VirusTotal (malicious vs. clean engine detections) and AbuseIPDB (confidence of abuse percentage).
  • Direct deep-links to external intelligence pages.

docs.title: Tab 6: 🛡️ SOAR Remediation
docs.text:
• Network Containment: Ready-to-execute Windows netsh advfirewall and Linux iptables rules to block malicious IPs and C2 domains.
  • EDR Host Isolation: API payloads for CrowdStrike Falcon and Microsoft Defender for Endpoint.
  • Custom Detection Signatures: Auto-authored Sigma and YARA rules to detect recurring instances of the attack.
  • Download Button: Export the full remediation plan as Markdown.

docs.title: Tab 7: 🔍 Threat Hunting
docs.text:
• Splunk SPL: Multi-index hunting queries scanning for observed process executions, C2 URLs, and beacon intervals.
  • Microsoft Sentinel KQL: Queries joining DeviceProcessEvents and DeviceNetworkEvents.
  • Elastic EQL: Process lineage queries tracing child-to-parent execution chains.
  • Download Button: Export queries as Markdown.

docs.title: Tab 8: 🎫 SOC Ticket
docs.text:
• Standardized, syntax-highlighted Jira / ServiceNow Incident API JSON payload with mapped incident priority, summary, timeline, and remediation recommendations.
  • Download Button: Export ticket payload as JSON.

docs.title: Tab 9: 📋 Report & STIX 2.1
docs.text:
• Full Forensic Report: Complete executive summary and technical analysis available for one-click Markdown download.
  • STIX 2.1 Bundle: Machine-readable OASIS Cyber Threat Intelligence JSON bundle containing indicator, malware, and observed-data objects for downstream TIP/SOAR ingestion.

docs.title: 📂 Reviewing Past Cases (Case History)
docs.text: In the sidebar, switch from 🆕 New Investigation to 📂 Case History: * View all previous investigations stored in the local SQLite database (data/sentinel.db). * Click 📂 View Report on any case to instantly restore the full dashboard, timeline, attack graph, and IOCs in milliseconds with zero LLM re-computation.

docs.title: ⚡ Headless Automated CLI Demo (run_demo.py)
docs.text:
If you want to evaluate the complete multi-agent pipeline from the terminal without opening a browser:

python run_demo.py

This runs the complete 7-agent pipeline across the sample EML, PCAP, and EVTX files in demo_data/ and saves the full report to demo_output.md.

docs.title: 🌐 REST API Usage (FastAPI)
docs.text:
For enterprise automation, SENTINEL exposes a full REST API:

uvicorn src.api:app --reload --port 8000

docs.title: Endpoints
docs.text:
• POST /api/v1/analyze: Upload evidence files and trigger background multi-agent investigation.
  • GET /api/v1/cases: Retrieve a list of all historical forensic cases.
  • GET /api/v1/cases/{case_id}: Retrieve detailed state, timeline, report, and IOCs for a specific case.
  • GET /health: Healthcheck endpoint.

Visit http://localhost:8000/docs for interactive Swagger/OpenAPI documentation.

docs.title: 🧪 Running Unit Tests
docs.text:
Run the full pytest suite to verify all forensic parsers and rule engines: 

pytest -v
All 10 tests should pass cleanly in under 1 second.
